lines.en: There’s a phrase I heard recently that made me stop and think for a little while.

It isn’t a new one, and this isn’t me saying it’s the first time I’ve heard it, but it is the first time that I’ve ever tried to seriously make sense of it, for it’s something I can’t seem to wrap my head around.
Love is in the air.
First and foremost, I applaud the creator of this phrase for framing love in a way that makes it sound like an airborne virus as that’s something I can actually relate to and agree with.
But what I don’t get is why everyone looks at this like a good thing.
No one is ever excited to catch a cold. And public opinion when it comes to the flu is even worse.
So why is this virus one that we all seem so determined to host? The air we breathe should remain clean at all times, should it not?
The existence of anything swimming or flying or living in the air is a terrifying concept, and it calls into question why more people don’t wear masks outside of the more popular pandemics.
Maybe I should start doing that.
Maybe covering my face would prevent me from falling for anyone who accidentally contaminates the air in the midst of some lukewarm debate on wires or the concept of breathing.
Because even if I don’t believe it’s love, my broken mind can’t help but display the symptoms of it.
It’s the same for everyone else who breathes on me and winds up getting tricked by the failure of their immune system into some state that makes their legs shake.
We’re all just sick.
So when I hear someone say that “love is in the air,” I can’t help but feel a little worried.
I can’t help but be a little scared — because there’s no way I can live without breathing, and I’m too cowardly to die at such a slow pace.
I can hold my breath as much as I want.
I can hide inside my home and hope the cracks beneath my doors suffice at keeping fresh air out.
But the rotting carcasses of those I’ve left behind are simply far too pungent now, and even masks and doors won’t keep their stench away from this cursed respiratory system.
I try to calm my nerves.
It never works.
There is only one thing that will.
: Okay, give me the hardest shit you’ve got.
: Go to the back room and take your pants off. I’ll be there with the lube in five. And I promise it’ll only hurt for the first ten minutes.
: Tough day?
: Every day is tough when you’ve lost the will to live.
: That’s where the pegging comes in. Why are you still here when you should be preparing your anus?
: That’s not- forget it. I’ll just fill a basket with anything I can find and hope that something works.
: Is your libido broken this time? Because Haruka is a self-proclaimed master when it comes to helping others re-find the horny. And maybe it’s your turn to be fixed instead of mine?
: I’m not looking to fix anybody right now. I’m just glad to see you’re still alive and well.
: I am not well at all, Haruka.
: Well hey, alive and unwell beats dead, doesn’t it?
: I don’t know. I’d say you could ask Maki’s husband, but I’m not sure you’d get a response.
: Nice.
: Ignoring the fact that I’m apparently the only one here without a morbid sense of humor, are you sure porn is the remedy to your missing will to live?
: There can be no remedy at this point, only distractions. So I will drown my sorrows in my own cum while my niece eats microwaved TV dinners and cries her eyes out a few walls over.
: That one was too real for me to laugh at. Sorry, Sensei.
: Go home and get some sleep, man. Because, as much as I want Maki’s shop to succeed, I feel like someone has to put their foot down right now and she’s way too much of a salesman to ever do that.
: I can only sleep so many hours, you know. What am I supposed to do with the rest of the day?
: I mean...you could just hang out with us as we’re both adults who have also endured hardship and wouldn’t judge you at any point for what you’re going through.

: She’s got a point, Sensei. And it’s kind of surprising that you haven’t really tried leaning on either of us at all during this extremely prolonged and sudden bout of sadness that no one understands but you.
: And hey, now that I’m a widow, you can even marry me if you want to take advantage of my health benefits and go seek out actual therapy instead or something.
: At the very least, that’d be the funniest way to cancel out the un-submitted marriage license your daughter has been holding over my head for months.
: The what?
: Did...Makoto trick you into signing a marriage license? Because she did something like that with me when she was little as well and I wouldn’t put it past her.
: Your...daughter made you fill out a marriage license?
: No, it was a recommendation letter for Harvard. She just asked to see my signature and then printed a whole ass form on top of it.
: Joke's on her, though. Harvard doesn’t give a shit what some mid-thirties porn dealer has to say. I don’t even know where Harvard is.
: Nowhere you have to worry about her actually going to so long as we’re all trapped in here. But, that’s enough about Makoto. Give me everything you’ve got.
: Are you robbing me now? Do I need to go get my rifle?
: You mean the horse dildo?
: Rifle. Horse cock. Same difference.
: I’m not robbing you. I’m just starting to feel normal by standing here and talking to you two and would like to crawl back into my hole and stop existing now.
: Heh. Hole.
: Is that why you never came to either of us? You want to feel miserable?
: Don’t you do the same thing when you’re upset?
: No, Haruka just calls upon everyone else for validation and attention until whatever’s causing her sadness goes away.
: Yeah. I never want to be sad. I just want people to feel bad for me. So, if that’s what you’re doing now-
: That’s not what I’m doing. I just don’t really know how to exist right now and it feels like everything I try to do makes things worse. So stasis seems like the only option.
: What about Ami, though?
: Yeah, what’s going on with her? Makoto said something about...organ harvesting recently?
: That sounds about right.
: Ami...isn’t doing so great.
: “Not great” as in refusing to eat and keeping herself locked in her room for days on end like Makoto did when Masahiro died? Or “not great” as in Haruka complaining about being lonely?
: Neither, really. She’s awake and conscious and replies to me when I speak to her, but she’s not leaving the house and seems just...completely dead inside.
: She’s been under a lot of mental stress lately and I’m pretty sure she’s blaming herself for the way I am. Which, on its own, would be one thing-
: But when combined with the fact that she’s already all sorts of fucked up from being raised by me, it makes things kind of snowball into some big clusterfuck that I don’t know what to do about.
: That just sounds like parenting, to be honest.
: Yeah, that’s the problem. I don’t know how to be a parent.
: You and me both, buddy.
: Have you tried asking Sara? She’s all about parenting stuff. Even if she occasionally medicates her teenage daughter with exorbitant amounts of alcohol.
: I haven’t. The only person I’ve really asked for help isn’t a parent either.
: Well, it’s no wonder why you’re still struggling then. Just talk to Sara. I’m sure she’ll have some idea of what to do to get Ami back to normal. And if she doesn’t-
: Go camping with us tomorrow.
: That is...a strange alternative to what Haruka just said.
: Come to think of it, that’s actually a great idea.
: Right? It’ll be just like the “Make Maki Horny Again” trip, but fractionally more depressing.
: And...how is camping going to make me a better parent, exactly? It’s not going to turn into some type of boot camp, is it?
: Not at all. A few of us girls were just looking to unwind and, since the weather’s been great lately, we figured we’d head out into the woods and try not to be eaten by bears.
: So what Maki’s suggesting is that you and Ami come along and try not to be eaten by bears too.
: Yeah! We can all avoid being eaten by bears together! Plus, Sara will be there and she might be able to help with the Ami situation.
: Sure. Except for the part where “the Ami situation” involves her not wanting to leave her room. There’s no way I can talk her into going camping. She’ll look at me like I’m insane.
: How can you be so sure? For all you know, Ami might have been waiting for you to do something like this for years.
: No harm in trying, right?
: Unless you don’t want to come, that is.
: Or you’re just afraid of bears.
Camping?...
I can’t say that’s...something I have much interest in, to tell you the truth. And I can’t imagine Ami would either given that she’s a girly-girl in practically every sense.
But...
Maybe this would be an opportunity to turn things around? For her.
My happiness comes second- and I’m not just saying that because I’ve all but abandoned it.
If Ami can find some semblance of normalcy in her life again...even if that normalcy comes in the form of something that wouldn’t be normal at all for us...
Maybe it would make pretending to be okay a little easier on my end?
: Well?
And maybe it would make her less afraid to open the door.
: I’ll...talk to her tonight.
: My parental genius knows no bounds! So long as it involves other people’s children and not my own.
: You think she’ll be okay with a bunch of women your age also being there?
: Not even slightly.
: Yeah, I didn’t think so.
: Like you said, though, there’s no harm in trying. And it’s a somewhat passive way for me to start ascending the steps to parenthood.
: That settles it, then! Sensei and Ami will come camping with us tomorrow!
: She hasn’t agreed yet, Maki...
: But she will!
: Maybe.
: Good enough for me! We’ll pick you up at 9:00.
: But-
: Just talk to her when you get home and give Maki a call when you find out.
: Worse comes to worst and she still drops by in the morning despite Ami not wanting to go, I can just restrain her and prevent her from honking.
: But I love honking the horn and I never get to do it! Don’t take this from me, Haruka!
I take it upon myself to sneak away as the two of them argue.
But, just when I think I’m safe, I wind up bumping into something else...
: Hey...
: How...are things?
: Oh, you know...
: Terrible.
: I see...
: Do you think they’ll maybe...stop being terrible soon?
: Probably not, to be honest...
: I see...
: Sensei, I-
: Are you going camping tomorrow?
: What?
: Camping...with your mom. Are you going?
: Are...are you going?
: I don’t know yet. Probably not.
: I’m trying to be a parent.
: A parent?
: Yeah.
: That’s...different.
: Yeah. Everything’s different now. And none of it’s really good.
: I figured as much on account of you not even showing up to the dorms anymore. And to think that all it took was something worse than the apocalypse in your eyes.
: I guess this means you’re a true member of the club now, huh?
: Yeah, I guess so. I’m not really sure what to do, though. Nothing I say about it sticks with anyone other than Ayane.
: Help her out, okay?
: Help her?
: Yeah. With how fucked I am right now, you’re kind of the only person she has to talk to about any of this since I just...don’t want to be bothered for the time being.
: And you think I do?
: No. But I know you’re enough of a teacher’s pet to do what I tell you.
: You’re not even my teacher anymore.
: I’ll always be your teacher and you know that.
: Makoto, I’m really sorry. I’ve got a lot of shit I have to figure out right now.
: You’ve had a lot of shit to figure out since the first time you walked into the classroom. The difference is that now you finally have to figure it out or we’ll all leave you behind.
: Maybe that’s for the best.
: It’s not.
: At least not for me. But new Makoto doesn’t have time to care about what anyone else wants as she’s too busy playing the game for the first time in her life.
: Still have that marriage license?
: Mhm. And no, you can’t have it.
: That’s fine.
: Is it?
: Yeah, hang on to it. It might come in handy one day.
: It might-
: If I need health benefits or something.
: Health...benefits?
: Are you coming camping tomorrow or not?
: Camping...right! I...
: I can’t...
: But maybe some other time-
: Yeah. Maybe some other time.
: Are you leaving? Already?...
: I’ll call you.
: Will you actually?...
: We’ll see.
: Only one way to find out.
